verdict.line: You lose if you trade into his Fury bar before level 6; you win once Stridebreaker is up and he has to burn E just to reach you.

brief.thesis: Renekton's Reign of Anger passive means every auto and Cull the Meek he lands builds toward 50 Fury, at which point Ruthless Predator becomes a 3-slash, shield-destroying, 1.5-second stun instead of a 0.75-second one — that's the entire reason he owns lane and solo-kill advantage in this matchup. Sett has zero hard CC until E (Facebreaker) unlocks at level 2 and no true burst until Haymaker's Grit is banked, so early trades are his to take. The 51.3% Sett win rate over 813 games only shows up once you survive to itemize, because Stridebreaker and Sett's own kit scale harder into extended fights than a Fury-dependent bruiser.

theirWindow.what: Ruthless Predator (W) upgrades to a 3-slash stun (1.5s, shield-destroying) instead of 0.75s, and Cull the Meek's damage and heal jump. He'll usually dash in with Slice and Dice (E) right after — back off or force him to spend it on a minion wave instead of you.

yourWindow.when: right after he dumps empowered W or E
yourWindow.what: Both go on full cooldown (W: 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s, E: 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s) and his Fury resets toward zero. Step in with your own E (Facebreaker) for the stun and cash out banked Grit on W (Haymaker) for the true-damage shield burst.

start.why: 52.2% win rate over 784 games and the dominant 79.8% pick — the extra sustain and damage matter because Renekton's Q (Cull the Meek) chips and heals him every time he swings near you.

boots.why: 50.1% win rate over 710 games and 77.1% pick — flat reduction on autos and his empowered W slashes is worth more here than magic resist since Renekton is fully physical.

core.why: First item spike that lets you actually stick to him instead of getting kited by Slice and Dice (E).
55.6% win rate over 124 games on this path — armor shred compounds with your Q's max-health damage on his tankier Dominus (R) form.
Sustain to outlast his Fury-fueled trades and keep your passive regen relevant when you're behind on health.

the lane is close and you need Facebreaker and Haymaker back faster to out-trade his cooldowns

runes.keystoneWhy: This page measures 55.4% win rate here — the third-hit burst lets you win short, sharp trades before he ever reaches 50 Fury, which is exactly the window you control.

summoners.why: 91.6% pick rate at 50.6% win rate — Ignite punishes his Cull the Meek healing directly and gives you kill pressure the moment his empowered-W all-in window closes.

playing.title: Don't feed his Fury bar
playing.detail: Every auto and Q he lands on you builds toward the 50-Fury threshold. Give up minions rather than trade autos with him level 1-2 if you don't have to.

playing.title: Hold E for a real stun
playing.detail: Facebreaker only stuns if enemies are on opposite sides of you — against a lone Renekton it just slows. Use minion positioning or wait for a real trade before committing it.

playing.title: Bank Grit before you punch
playing.detail: Haymaker stores damage you take as Grit passively. Let a poke or two land, then cash it in for the shield and true-damage burst rather than using W on cooldown.

playing.title: Walk him down after his E
playing.detail: Slice and Dice is his only real disengage/engage tool and it's down for 16-10 seconds depending on rank. Press when it's gone.

playing.title: Look for the level 6 all-in
playing.detail: The Show Stopper slams him down and slows everyone near the landing — use it to drag him off his wave or away from turret range for a clean kill attempt.

playing.title: Play for tempo, not for level 1-5 trades
playing.detail: You're not favored in isolated early trades. Farm safe, force him to spend Fury on the wave, and let Stridebreaker do the talking from level 9-10 onward.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and win rates above are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch; the mechanical reasoning and timing calls are my own read of the ability text, not measured data.

stats.opponentTip: Keep an eye out on Renekton’s Fury before fighting him. Use [W] when he tries using his reinforced skill to gain the upper hand in combat.
